source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL short prose passage in English, set in the target scenario below. It must be
a HOMEOSYNTACTIC transposition of a hidden source: hold the source's syntactic form at the level
specified below while inventing entirely new words and moving the content into the target
scenario. It is NOT a paraphrase or a translation.

Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE-NESTING SCHEMA below --- an indented tree in which each line is a clause (main / relative / adverbial / complement / coordinate) and indentation marks subordination (a clause indented under another is embedded in it). Hold the SAME nesting: the same clauses, each embedded under the same kind of parent clause, to the same depth. The WORD ORDER and the words themselves are entirely yours; only the clause-embedding tree is fixed.

    - relative/adnominal clause

Period 7 (about 12 words) clause-nesting schema:

  - main clause

TARGET SCENARIO --- render the content here (in your own words):
  - an airport/border security checkpoint at a busy hour
  - the queue and the barriers; the divestment of belongings into trays
  - the scanners, metal detectors, and the body-search gesture
  - an officer and a traveller singled out of the line; documents and a wanded pat-down
  - the register of control: instructions, signage, the impersonal courtesy of authority

REQUIREMENTS --- both hold together:
1. CLAUSE NESTING PRESERVED --- the same clause-embedding tree per period (which clause embeds in which, to the same depth), in any word order and words you choose.
2. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible passage in the target scenario; new lexicon,

Write modern, natural English. Produce the 10 periods in order as continuous prose --- no
numbering, no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

Passengers filed through the bustling security checkpoint at the airport,  
to pass each one had to divest their belongings into trays before proceeding,  
in line stood a traveler whose turn it was now,  
at this moment an officer approached him with a questioning gaze, demanding documents and initiating a pat-down search,  
with every instruction issued, clear signage directed the flow of people through the checkpoint,  
for each person selected for closer inspection, a thorough examination became necessary to ensure security,  
underneath the watchful eyes of the officers, travelers moved past metal detectors and scanners efficiently,  
in the midst of all, one could see the organized chaos that was part of this daily routine,  
among the travelers singled out for additional scrutiny, a detailed process unfolded involving a wand sweep followed by a more invasive search procedure,  
for every traveler who entered, an intricate system of checks and balances ensured safety.

Passengers waited anxiously by the checkpoint,  
to be screened thoroughly,  
while machines whirred and beeped incessantly.  
The officer who was in charge of security,  
knew that each traveler’s belonging must be checked carefully.  
Every item needed to be examined closely,
so that nothing suspicious could slip past unnoticed.
Instructions were posted prominently throughout the area,
reminding everyone about the necessary procedures.
As one individual stepped forward from the crowd,
the officer requested their documents and conducted a thorough search,
directing them through another series of steps,
all designed to maintain strict adherence to protocol.

Amidst the bustling hubbub at the airport security checkpoint, where travellers jostle through metal detectors and x-ray machines, one individual was singled out for a more thorough inspection by an officer.
